/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 22 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3432 (33)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5892 (53)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2299 (44)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1776 (5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 997 (4)
CAPESIZE
The BCI 182 5TC rose by a further $488 today to $53,441, although the transpacific round voyage appeared under some pressure. The C5 route had been expected to climb to $17 or higher after fixtures were reportedly concluded in the high $16s later yesterday. However, despite the presence of two miners, the west Australia to Qingdao run instead slipped by $0.135 to $16.73. The C3 index remained firm at $43.427 for mid-October loading, supporting a $1,295 increase in return for the China/Brazil or West Africa round voyage to $53,004. Sentiment in the Atlantic basin continued to strengthen, with a healthy volume of cargoes in the market including both transatlantic and fronthaul trades.

Atlantic
Glovis was rumoured to have taken a TBN for 170,000/10 Tubarao to Qingdao 18/24 October at $43.70.

Asia
There was talk of Rio Tinto taking more than one vessel for their 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao basis 8/10 October at $16.50. FMG was also linked to taking vessels for 160,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao on earlier and tighter laycans at tick higher levels. Last night, the GH Leveche (179,223 2009) was taken by Vale for 170,000/10 TRMT to Qingdao 30 September /2 October at a rate in the very high $12s.
PANAMAX
Brokers have reported an increase in trans-Atlantic demand today, with higher fixing rates being circulated and bid levels said to be moving upwards. As a result, the P1A posted gains on the day. Fronthaul sentiment is also described as positive by market sources, although activity has not matched the levels seen in the trans-Atlantic market. Demand from EC South America is reportedly stronger than in previous days, leading to discussions of firmer numbers on the P6 route. Market participants have also noted a widening bid-offer spread, as Owners raise their rate expectations while Charterers maintain more consistent bidding levels. In the Pacific, sentiment is described as drifting, with prompt demand from Indonesia reported to have eased. Despite this, Owners are said to be holding firm on their rate expectations for the longer Australia and North Pacific round voyages. Market participants have noted that while demand from both Australia and the North Pacific remains steady, the continued abundance of available tonnage is limiting any meaningful upward movement in rates and preventing stronger gains from materialising. The P5TC marked an increase of $390 to $20,687.

Atlantic
The New Excellence (79,449 2014) open Krishnapatnam 22 September was reported to have been placed on subject’s basis APS EC South America 22/25 October for an Atlantic trip with iron ore at $30,000 to Worthington. The Aries Star (81,895 2020) open Hazira 25/30 September was also said to have been placed on subjects for an EC South America fronthaul at $25,000, with the scrubber benefit for the Charterers.

Asia
The scrubber-fitted Miranda (82,028 2026) open Gunsan 24/25 September was reported fixed for a trip via EC Australia to India with coal, to LSS, with the scrubber benefit for Charterers’ account. Market sources suggested the fixture concluded at a rate somewhere between $23,500 and $25,000, although there was some debate regarding the final level agreed. The Lime Alina (84,990 2022) open Tianjin 24 September, Tiger North (76,213 2013) open Masinloc 23 September, and Tai Kudos (82,008 2017) open Batangas 23 September were all reported on subjects, with no further details reported. The S'Hail Lusail (86,041 2007) open Lanshan 22 September was said to have been placed on subjects to Pan Ocean at $19,000 for a trip via Gladstone to South Korea and the Nord Draco (84,694 2014) open Bahodopi 28 September was said to be on subjects with Fullinks for an Australia round.
SUPRAMAX
Another sluggish day with the market looking for direction. The BSI rose 5 points again to 1,776, and the 11TC average was up $54 to settle at $22,443.
Demand from the US Gulf has slowed, although this could be an end of month correction, whilst the South Atlantic seemed slightly better, maybe influenced by other sizes. Sentiment was said to remain positive from the Continent and Mediterranean, but very little has emerged so far. Holidays in Asia might have contributed to the slow start there, but levels being discussed appear unchanged, with certain trades positional and bucking the trend at higher levels. The Rosita I (66,200 2026) ex yard Hong Kong prompt fixed a trip Chittagong with limestone at $29,000 and the Attiki SB (60,900 2015) Ulsan 24-26 September agreed a trip into the US Gulf in the $16,000’s, but in both cases a Charterer wasn’t mentioned. The Vosco Defender (55,885 2011) Villanueva 29-30 September went on subjects for a trip via East Kalimantan to Thailand at $20,000, again to an unnamed source.
HANDYSIZE
The market showed little change in overall dynamics, with sentiment remaining largely positional. The BHSI closed at 997, while the 7TC average edged up by $71 to finish at $17,947. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, rates remained largely flat, with limited activity reported. The South Atlantic held steady, while the US Gulf remained highly active, with sentiment continuing to appear firm. The Pacific market was quiet but stable, as several holidays across Asia limited activity and no clear direction emerged.

Atlantic
The Ocean Helios (40,076 2026) was reported placed on subjects for a trip from SW Pass via the Mississippi River to the WC Central America with grains at $28,000 by ADM, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Rossana (39,935 2016) open prompt in CJK was fixed for a trip to the WC Central America at $21,500, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Indian Infrastructure Sector Growth

India’s output across eight core infrastructure sectors recorded 4.8% growth in August, easing from 5% in July and recording a four-month low, newswires report from official data. Strong expansion in cement, electricity and iron ore was partly offset by contractions in coal, natural gas, crude oil and fertilisers. The steel and cement sectors climbed a respective 3.4% and 12.5% while coal output declined 3.8% in the period.
